claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a disordered BCC structure.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The high Mo content of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo produces electronegativity differences that limit plasticity.
Controlled sub-solvus annealing and cooling will nucleate a fine dispersion of Mo-rich precipitates without substantial coarsening.
Light deformation may assist the proposed precipitation treatment.
Processing at approximately 0.5–0.6 Tm will remain below the temperature at which significant recrystallization or coarse second-phase formation occurs.
An inert atmosphere will avoid oxidation during the heat treatment.
Fine Mo-rich precipitates will mitigate local electronegativity differences in NbZrTiHfMo.
Mitigation of local electronegativity differences will alter microstructural stress fields and enhance dislocation mobility.
Mo-rich clusters or precipitates will relieve internal stress concentrations and improve plastic flow.
The Mo-rich precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion and thereby preserve yield strength.
Mitigating the locally adverse effects of Mo clustering will enhance ductility.
The treatment will increase compressive strain-to-failure by approximately 15% or more relative to the untreated alloy.
After treatment, compressive yield strength will remain within 10% of 1719 MPa.
The beneficial effect will occur only within a narrow annealing time-temperature window.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration will cause precipitate coarsening or unwanted phase formation.
Precipitate coarsening or unwanted phase formation will reduce strength or increase brittleness.
